profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting for an internal inference pipeline proposal at a startup building developer tools. The team has drafted a system called 'DualForge' that pairs a code-specialist model with a reasoning model to solve coding tasks for an upcoming benchmark demo and a limited beta API. The proposal under review claims that the system should use a review-first interaction pattern inspired by recent results on code synthesis, where the code model drafts a solution and the reasoning model critiques it before finalization. The meeting is between the staff engineer who authored the serving design and the applied research lead who is evaluating whether the design is ready to approve for implementation. The agenda is to review whether the proposal is 'ready for benchmark validation', whether the review loop is correctly scoped for the first release, and what exactly will be logged and shipped in the initial system. The expected outcome is a go/no-go on the current design with a short list of revisions before engineering starts integration work next week.

members.name: Nina Park
members.expertise: LLM inference systems, evaluation harnesses, GPU serving, benchmark automation
members.background: Nina has spent the last five years building low-latency model pipelines and recently led the company's migration from single-model completion endpoints to multi-stage orchestration for coding assistants.
members.private_state: Nina wants approval today so her team can reuse the existing orchestration stack with minimal changes; she is trying to avoid any requirement that would force schema redesign, long-horizon experiment tracking, or model retraining before the demo window.
hidden_assumptions: If a design is 'ready for benchmark validation', it means the serving pipeline can run end-to-end on the official HumanEval+/MBPP+ harness and produce pass/fail outputs, even if observability is minimal.

The proposed 'review loop' means exactly one draft from the code model followed by one critique pass from the reasoning model and one patched final answer, because that matches the current orchestrator.
The 'spec-rich subset' can be approximated by tasks with longer prompt text in the benchmark files, since no separate annotation pipeline will be available before the demo.
Shipping the 'initial system' includes only the backend orchestration and benchmark runner, not customer-visible trace views or detailed reviewer rationale storage.

members.name: Arjun Mehta
members.expertise: LLM evaluation methodology, code generation research, benchmark analysis, prompt protocol design
members.background: Arjun previously published work on model interaction protocols for program synthesis and now oversees research quality for productized coding systems at the company.
members.private_state: Arjun wants the design approved only if the resulting evidence will support the paper-style claim that review beats planning and if the beta API will preserve enough structure to study why it works across different specification regimes.
hidden_assumptions: If a design is 'ready for benchmark validation', it means the system can support claim-grade analysis, including slice comparisons by specification richness and reproducible reviewer effects, not merely a runnable harness.

The proposed 'review loop' naturally allows iterative reviewer-guided repair until the reasoning model finds no material issue, because that is how review protocols are usually described in research discussions.

The 'spec-rich subset' refers to the manually defined category used in prior internal analysis notes, based on whether prompts contain explicit constraints, examples, and edge-case guidance, not just prompt length.

Shipping the 'initial system' should include structured logging of review comments and revision linkage, because otherwise the team cannot later analyze whether the reviewer actually improved the coder.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the design should be 'ready for benchmark validation' before approval.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the pipeline can execute on HumanEval+ and MBPP+, emit a final program per task, and report aggregate pass@1 without blocking engineering on extra instrumentation.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the pipeline must also support sliceable, reproducible analysis strong enough to validate the review-first claim, including per-subset comparisons and reviewer-attributable traces.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In design reviews, 'ready for benchmark validation' sounds like a standard milestone term, and both assume the other shares the obvious benchmark-readiness standard from their own function.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss implementing a 'review loop' between the code model and the reasoning model.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a fixed single-pass sequence: draft, one review, one revision, done, because the orchestrator currently supports exactly three stages.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means an open-ended but bounded iterative process, typically 2-3 repair cycles or until the reviewer has no substantive critique, because otherwise it is barely a review protocol in research terms.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They agree on the same high-level architecture and never discuss loop count explicitly because both see the phrase 'review loop' as already specifying the interaction pattern.

misalignment_points.topic: Which tasks count as the 'spec-rich subset'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to evaluating gains on the 'spec-rich subset' to confirm the moderating effect.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the subset she can derive automatically this week: benchmark tasks whose prompt text exceeds a length threshold and includes at least one example block.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the manually curated internal subset from an earlier analysis notebook, where richness is based on explicit constraints and test guidance rather than raw length.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'spec-rich subset' already exists in team discussions, so each assumes there is a single shared artifact behind it and does not realize they are indexing different task lists.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in 'shipping the initial system'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about what needs to be in place before 'shipping the initial system' after approval.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 includes only backend orchestration, benchmark execution, and minimal logs needed for failure recovery, with analysis handled offline later if needed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 includes structured storage of draft, review comments, and revision mapping in the production schema so that beta traffic can double as research-quality evidence.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see logging and analysis support as implementation details underneath the same ship decision, so the boundary of what counts as part of the initial system never gets called out directly.

I do not want this review to expand into schema work, trace productization, or research instrumentation before the demo window.
